intro: This course covered why, how and when to report accidents, incidents and near misses factually, and the legal duties behind reporting.
points: People come first — make the area safe, check for injuries, give first aid within your training, and call 999 without delay if someone is seriously hurt.
Report every near miss — it is a free warning that costs nothing but can prevent real harm.
Record factually and promptly, ideally before your shift ends — write what you saw and did, not opinions or blame, then sign and date it.
RIDDOR requires the responsible person to report serious work-related events to the HSE, so always pass information up the line.
Under the duty of candour (Regulation 20), be open and honest with the person affected, give a truthful account, and apologise.
A no-blame culture looks for the root cause, not a culprit — and incident records must be kept secure under UK GDPR.
